_comment: FAKE EXPERT-REVIEW SIMULATION ONLY. All questions, responses, reviewers, labels, and decisions are synthetic. This file is not authorized research evidence and must not be used to claim expert agreement, calibration, feasibility, or educational effectiveness.

cases.question_item: Synthetic item A: combine two unlike fractional quantities.
cases.example_learner_response: The learner combines both top and bottom values directly.

independent_reviews.reason_for_label: The response follows the synthetic direct-combination error pattern.
The same synthetic operation is applied to both parts without transformation.

cases.adjudication_reason: Synthetic reviewers agree on the primary label.

cases.question_item: Synthetic item B: compare two representations of the same quantity.
cases.example_learner_response: The learner selects the representation with the larger visible denominator.

independent_reviews.reason_for_label: The choice appears driven by a single surface value.
The synthetic response is consistent with surface-value comparison.

cases.adjudication_reason: Synthetic reviewers agree, while retaining ambiguity in alternatives.

cases.question_item: Synthetic item C: continue a rule-based sequence.
cases.example_learner_response: The learner gives an answer without a stable observable rule.

independent_reviews.reason_for_label: One response is insufficient to distinguish guessing from a stable misconception.
The response might reflect applying only the most recent difference.

cases.adjudication_reason: Synthetic disagreement is resolved conservatively to abstention.

cases.question_item: Synthetic item D: identify the operation needed in a short scenario.
cases.example_learner_response: The learner uses addition where the scenario requires grouping equally.

independent_reviews.reason_for_label: The selected operation does not represent equal grouping.
The response consistently maps the story to the wrong operation family.

cases.adjudication_reason: Synthetic reviewers independently agree on the primary operation error.
